_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Unless a grain of wheat falls and dies, it remains alone.
But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
The cross is foolishness to the perishing.
To us it is the power and the wisdom of God.
Walk while you have the light.
We will follow the light of the world. Come, let us worship.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: A single grain of wheat lies in your hand; keep it whole and it stays alone, but bury it in the dark earth and it breaks open into harvest.
The hour has come.
Now his soul is troubled, and still he will not turn back; the foolishness of the cross is the wisdom of God.
The hour has come.
Greeks and strangers press in: we wish to see Jesus. Lifted up, he will draw the whole world to himself.
The hour has come.
Walk while you have the light, before the night falls; believe in the light and become children of light. Come, let us worship.
The hour has come. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Unless a grain of wheat falls and dies, it bears no fruit.
The hour has come.
The cross is foolishness to some, but to us the power of God.
The hour has come.
Walk while you have the light; come, let us worship.
The hour has come. Amen.
